Course project

About

Campus Placement Prep Assistant is a prompt-engineering project for Indian college students preparing for campus placements.

What the project does

A student can talk to a mentor, sit a one-question-at-a-time mock interview, take a generated aptitude quiz, paste a resume for an ATS-style review, and read a short hiring outline for common campus recruiters. Progress is a chart of scores saved in the browser.

The interesting part for this course is not a custom model. It is how the prompts are written: a role, an example, a hidden checklist before a score, a strict JSON shape, and rules that keep the bot on placement prep.

AI tools used

  • Google Gemini

    The language model. The server calls gemini-3.8-flash (or GEMINI_MODEL) with the free-tier API key. The browser never sees the key.

  • Next.js route handlers

    Four routes shape the request: /api/chat streams text. /api/interview, /api/aptitude, and /api/resume ask for JSON.

  • lib/prompts.ts

    Every system prompt lives here, with a comment naming the technique. Swapping a prompt does not require a UI change.

  • localStorage

    Chat history and scores stay on the device. There is no database and no user account.

Prompt techniques used

Prompt techniques, where they are used, and why
TechniqueWhereWhy it is here
Role promptingEvery chat mode, quiz writer, interviewer, and resume reviewerThe model is given a specific job (mentor, interviewer, coach, reviewer) so the tone and task stay stable.
Few-shotAptitude Coach chat mode and the quiz JSON promptOne worked example shows the exact question shape and explanation style we want copied.
Chain-of-thoughtInterview scoring and resume scoringThe prompt tells the model which checks to make before it picks a number. The checks stay out of the JSON the UI renders.
Output-format constraintsChat markdown, and JSON for quizzes, interviews, and resumesThe UI can trust keys like score and answerIndex. Invalid JSON is rejected and requested once more.
GuardrailsEvery system promptThe chatbot stays on placements and career prep, refuses unrelated requests, and does not invent hiring outcomes.
